Lesson 029: texture memory, compression and mip streaming

    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    What this shows
    
    
    
      
    Price it before it ships
    Width × height × bytes per pixel × 4/3. A raw 2048² terrain texture is 21.33 MB; twelve of them are more than the whole streaming budget.
    
      
    Compression stays compressed
    ASTC is decoded by the GPU on every read, so it is 4× smaller in memory than RGBA32, not only on disk. The price is a small loss of quality and slow encoding.
    
      
    Streaming trades memory for time
    Only the mips the camera needs stay in memory. A fixed budget keeps the app safe, but under pressure some houses stay soft, and new mips arrive a fraction of a second late.
    
    
    
    
    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses the lesson's numbers: 1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes, mips add 4/3, the rest of the game uses 600 MB, the low-end phone is killed at about 1,100 MB and the mid-range one at about 1,800 MB (real limits move with other apps), and storage delivers about 80 MB/s. A real streamer picks mips per texture from screen size every frame, loads them over several frames and has its own priorities.
